subject.title: fix(plugins): keep run context available after registration

question: Should the public plugin lifecycle contract explicitly allow run-context operations after register returns while denying all run-context access from a replaced or inactive registry?
rationale: The code and tests support this symmetric ownership boundary, but changing observable behavior for stale plugin instances is a compatibility-sensitive plugin API decision that requires owner intent.

options.title: Confirm the symmetric lifecycle contract
options.body: Accept active post-registration access and inactive-registry denial, then require one redacted installed-plugin runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve stale read behavior
options.body: Revise the patch to leave inactive-registry reads available, accepting that retired plugin instances can observe replacement-owned state while writes remain blocked.

options.title: Pause the API change
options.body: Hold the PR until the broader plugin reload and stale-callback lifecycle contract is documented and reviewed together.

recommendation.title: Confirm the symmetric lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Accept active post-registration access and inactive-registry denial, then require one redacted installed-plugin runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The release and review-routing evidence makes steipete the best available owner for a public plugin SDK lifecycle decision.
